items.body:
## Bug Description

The `cronjob` tool's `action=update` cannot pin a job's `provider`/`model`, even though (a) the handler function accepts those parameters and (b) the cron drift-guard's own skip remediation instructs the operator to pass them.

When an unpinned agent-cron job is skipped by the "unintended spend" drift guard, the delivered alert says:

> Pin it explicitly: `cronjob action=update job_id=<id> provider=<provider> model=<model>`.

Following that instruction returns:

```
{"error": "No updates provided.", "success": false}
```

…because `provider` and `model` are not in the tool's JSON schema, so the runtime drops them and the handler receives `None` for both → `updates` is empty → the "No updates provided" early return fires.

## Root cause

`tools/cronjob_tools.py` has a three-way inconsistency:

1. **Handler signature accepts them** — `_cronjob_tool(...)` declares `model: Optional[str] = None` and `provider: Optional[str] = None` (lines ~1155–1156), and the `update` branch populates `updates["model"]` / `updates["provider"]` from them.
2. **The exposed `CRONJOB_SCHEMA` (line ~1558) omits them.** Its `properties` block contains only 16 keys — `action, attach_to_session, context_from, deliver, enabled_toolsets, job_id, monitor_script, monitor_url, name, no_agent, prompt, repeat, schedule, script, skills, workdir` — and none of `model`, `provider`, `base_url`, `reason`, `skill`.
3. **The drift-skip remediation text (`cron/scheduler.py`) explicitly tells operators to pass `provider=` and `model=`** on `cronjob action=update`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create (or already have) an agent cron job with no pinned model/provider.
2. Change the global `model.default` (or provider) so the job's inherited inference config drifts from its creation-time snapshot.
3. Wait for the next tick → job is skipped and the drift alert is delivered.
4. Run exactly what the alert says:
   `cronjob action=update job_id=<id> provider=<provider> model=<model>`
5. Observe: `{"error": "No updates provided.", "success": false}`.

## Expected Behavior

The remediation command in the alert should work. `provider`/`model` (and ideally `base_url`, `reason`, `skill` — the other handler params missing from the schema) should be exposed in `CRONJOB_SCHEMA` so `action=update` can actually pin inference config.

## Actual Behavior

The params are silently dropped (not in schema), the handler sees `None`, and the update is rejected with "No updates provided". Operator has to bypass the tool entirely (e.g. call `cron.jobs.update_job` directly) to pin the model.

## Environment

- Repo: NousResearch/hermes-agent
- Commit: `45af7a71fc` (`fmt(js): \`npm run fix\` on merge (#86935)`)
- Reproduced on the default profile (Linux), Telegram gateway session.

items.title: [Bug]: Bot Mode rows from a remote gateway open through the local profile route and spawn a local backend
items.body:
### Bug Description

With Hermes Desktop connected to a self-hosted gateway over a URL remote (per-profile
remote override, top-level connection mode "local"), the Bots pane correctly lists the
REMOTE profiles — the roster comes from profiles.list on the active gateway. But clicking
a bot does not open a chat on that gateway. Any bot whose name has no matching entry in
the local connection.json falls through to the local routing table's last case and Desktop
spawns a brand-new local backend with that name (`hermes --profile <name> serve`) on the
client machine, creating ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>.

The row hangs while that empty local agent boots. If it finishes, you are talking to a
fresh local agent that shares nothing but the name with the remote bot you clicked.

This hits every sub-profile on the remote gateway, since those never have a local
connection.json entry. The main profile only works by accident, when the user happens to
have created a same-named Desktop profile pointing at that URL.

Related but distinct from #82530 / #82536 (REST profile scoping on mapped backends).
This one is UI routing: the roster and the open path disagree about which backend owns
the profile.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Self-host a Hermes gateway at https://agent.example.com with a named main profile and
   at least one sub-profile (e.g. `main-agent` and `ingester`).
2. In Hermes Desktop, leave the global connection mode at "local" and add a Desktop
   profile with mode "remote" pointing at https://agent.example.com. Sign in.
3. Open the Bots pane. The roster correctly lists the REMOTE profiles, including
   `ingester`.
4. Click the `ingester` bot row.
5. Watch ~/.hermes/profiles/ on the client machine.

### Expected Behavior

Clicking a bot row opens that bot's canonical "Bot Chat" on the backend the roster
row came from — the remote gateway that answered profiles.list.

If Desktop genuinely cannot route to that profile, it should say so. Silently
materializing a same-named local agent is worse than an error, because the chat looks
like it worked.

### Actual Behavior

The row hangs. Desktop resolves the profile name against the LOCAL connection.json,
finds no entry, and spawns a local backend for it. A new ~/.hermes/profiles/<name>
directory appears on the client machine. No request ever reaches the remote gateway.

Selecting the same gateway via its profile chip works normally — that path is the
active/primary profile and skips re-resolution entirely.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Not sharing a `hermes debug share` bundle — the report includes my gateway hostnames,
dashboard OAuth client IDs and log contents, and this is a self-hosted setup on a
private domain. Environment details are filled in below, and the root cause is traced
in the source at the commit named there, so the bundle would not add anything relevant
to this bug. Happy to answer specific questions or run a targeted command.
```

### Operating System

macOS 26.5.2

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

v0.20.2 (2026.8.16), install method git, HEAD cecb3a6ed7

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The roster and the open path resolve the profile against two different sources of truth.

Roster (correct):
  apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js:2040
    const local = await host.request('profiles.list', {})
  -> names come from the ACTIVE gateway (the remote one).

Rows are only tagged `remoteSource` when they arrive via the host.agents() union
(mergeMultiSourceRoster, plugin.js:2078). Rows from profiles.list are untagged, so
BotRow skips the ensureAgent branch at plugin.js:3089 that would activate the owning
connection first.

Open path (resolves locally):
  plugin.js:2246          host.openSession(id, { profile: name })
  sdk/index.ts:330        await ensureGatewayProfile(profile)
  store/profile.ts:292    ensureGatewayProfile -> ensureGatewayForProfile
  store/gateway.ts:661    not primary; sharedPrimaryRoute() is false because the
                          top-level connection mode is "local" (globalRemoteActive()
                          returns false), so route 3 never applies
                       -> createSecondary(key) -> openSecondary -> Electron ensureBackend

  electron/connection-config.ts:511  resolveProfileBackendRoute(), four routes:
      1. profile == primary                -> primary backend
      2. per-profile remote override       -> pooled remote descriptor
      3. global remote                     -> primary, scoped per request
      4. anything else                     -> pooled LOCAL backend

  A profile that exists only on the remote matches none of 1-3, so it takes route 4.

  electron/main.ts, spawnPoolBackend():
      const remote = opts.forceLocal ? null : await resolveRemoteBackend(profile)
      ...
      const backendArgs = ['--profile', profile, 'serve', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '0']

  resolveRemoteBackend() returns null (no connection.json entry, no global remote), so
  Desktop spawns a local child for a name it only ever saw on a remote roster.

The gap: route 4 is the correct default for a name typed into the local profile
switcher, but it is never correct for a name that came from a remote gateway's
profiles.list. resolveProfileBackendRoute() has no way to know the difference, because
the row's origin is dropped between the roster and openSession.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

1. Preserve row provenance. When useRoster() builds rows from the active gateway's
   profiles.list, tag them with that gateway's connection id (the registry id when the
   active connection is a registry source), the same way mergeMultiSourceRoster tags
   union rows. BotRow's existing ensureAgent(bot.connectionId, bot.name) branch at
   plugin.js:3089 then routes them to the backend that actually owns their state.db —
   the machinery is already there, the rows just aren't labelled.

2. Make route 4 refuse to invent. resolveProfileBackendRoute()'s local fallback should
   not apply to a profile that arrived from a remote roster. Passing the origin through
   would let it return an error instead of spawning `hermes --profile <name> serve` for
   a name that has no local existence. An explicit "profile <name> lives on <host>, not
   on this machine" beats a silent empty local agent.

Either half alone stops the data loss; (1) is the one that makes remote bots actually
chattable.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [UX]: Always-visible connection picker in status bar for quick local↔SSH/backend switching
items.body:
## Problem

When connected to a remote backend (SSH), Hermes Desktop shows a **connection indicator button** in the bottom-left status bar that allows switching back to local with one click. However, when running in **pure local mode**, this button does not exist — there is no way to quickly initiate a remote connection from the UI.

The only path to switch from local → SSH is:
1. Open Settings
2. Navigate to Gateway
3. Select SSH connection
4. Click Apply

This creates an **asymmetrical UX**: SSH→Local is one click, Local→SSH is 4+ steps through settings.

## Use Case

Users who frequently switch between local work and remote VPS/SSH sessions (a very common workflow for sysadmins and developers) need a fast, always-accessible way to initiate connections without diving into settings each time.

## Proposed Solution

An **optional, always-visible connection picker** in the status bar (similar to the existing SSH indicator, but bidirectional):



Key properties:
- **Optional toggle** — users can enable/disable it in settings
- **Always visible** (when enabled), not just when connected remotely
- **Shows all configured backends** (local, SSH, remote URL, Docker, etc.)
- **One-click switch** — same convenience in both directions
- **Persistent state** — remembers the last selection

## Context

- Related to #71257 (multi-backend Desktop) — this is a focused UX improvement on the same axis
- Bug #84599 (SSH silent fallback to local) is a known issue that makes the current SSH workflow fragile; this picker wouldn't fix that bug but would make the manual workaround (re-initiating the connection) much faster
- The existing status bar connection indicator only works one way (remote→local); this proposal makes it bidirectional

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop v0.20.0
- OS: Linux (KDE Plasma)
- Use case: switching between local development and remote VPS administration

items.body:
## Bug Description

The repository contains two files under `contributors/emails/` that differ only by the case of one letter:

- `contributors/emails/agent@Agents-Mac-mini.local`  -> `skip-agent`
- `contributors/emails/agent@agents-Mac-mini.local`  -> `momomojo`

Both are present at the tip of `main` (introduced together in `17fa4e294`).

On case-insensitive filesystems (Windows, and macOS by default), these two paths collide: they map to a single file on disk, but git tracks two distinct index entries with different contents. The working tree therefore can never be clean — `git status` always reports one of the two as modified.

## Impact

Every `hermes update` on Windows detects this dirty state and takes the auto-stash path, printing `-> Local changes detected - stashing before update...` even though the user changed nothing. This produces a spurious warning (and a stash/restore cycle) on every update.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Clone the repo on Windows (or any case-insensitive filesystem): `git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git`
2. Run `git status` immediately after the clone finishes.

## Expected Behavior

`nothing to commit, working tree clean`

## Actual Behavior

`git status` reports one of the two case-variant files as `modified`, permanently.

## Proposed Fix

Remove one of the two duplicate entries. They represent the same email (differing only in case) but map it to two different logins (`skip-agent` vs `momomojo`), which looks like an accidental duplicate — a maintainer should confirm which mapping is intended and delete the other.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Hermes: v0.20.2

items.title: [Bug]: Bots pane duplicates every bot on remote-gateway-only desktops; rows multiply on each interaction
items.body:
### What happens

On a desktop whose ONLY backend is one **remote gateway** (no local profiles on the desktop machine), the Bots pane shows every bot **twice** immediately after launch, and the copies then **keep growing** with each UI interaction — unbounded — until the app is restarted. Restart resets to the 2× baseline.

### Repro

1. Run the gateway on a headless server. Connect a Hermes Desktop on a different machine via remote gateway (the desktop has no local profiles).
2. Create a couple of bots (or just observe the built-in roster).
3. Open the Bots pane → every bot appears exactly twice.
4. Click unrelated buttons in the app (any interaction that causes a repaint/refetch). Each interaction adds another full copy of every bot to the list. Growth is unbounded.
5. Restart the desktop app → back to exactly 2 copies per bot.

### Suspected cause

`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`, `useRoster()` + `mergeMultiSourceRoster()` (introduced by 8236b4177 "feat: sync bundled Bot Mode with multi-source roster"):

- `profiles.list` against the ACTIVE (remote) gateway returns the roster once.
- `host.agents()` union roster then re-supplies the same agents. Because they arrive through a remote connection, `connectionKind !== 'local'`, so the merge treats them as rows from *other sources* and pushes a duplicate row for each.

On a remote-gateway-only desktop, the active gateway and the union describe the SAME agents, but the merge assumes local and non-local sources are disjoint sets. The 2× baseline follows directly.

The unbounded growth on interaction is a second defect — likely the roster accumulating across refetch/repaint cycles (refetchInterval 5s + `gatewayUp`-triggered refetches + `ctx.register` calls without idempotency guards), but the baseline duplication is the structural bug worth fixing first.

### Environment

- hermes-agent v0.20.2 (2026.8.16), git install, pulled 2026-08-17 (plugin.js at 8236b4177 head)
- Desktop: Linux (Steam Deck, desktop app)
- Gateway: headless Linux server, reached over remote gateway; desktop has no local profiles
- 3 profiles on the gateway (default + 2 named) — all duplicated identically

### Expected

One row per bot regardless of connection topology; interactions must never multiply roster rows.

### Suggested fix direction

Key the union merge on (connectionId, profile) rather than connectionKind, and dedupe the merged result against the active gateway's own connection before appending. Cap roster identity so repaints cannot accumulate rows.

items.title: Bot Mode: deleting a bot on Windows always fails with WinError 32 (desktop backend holds the profile's memory_store.db open)

items.body:
## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 11 (native, git-bash shell)
- **Hermes**: v0.20.2 (2026.8.16), installed at `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent`, Python 3.11.15
- **Surface**: Hermes Desktop (win-unpacked Electron build), Bot Mode plugin enabled (default)
- **Profiles**: `default` (primary), plus `default-2`, `default-3`, `fitness`, `llm-wiki`

## Summary

On Windows, deleting any non-default profile **always fails** with `PermissionError: [WinError 32]` because the desktop's backend process (`hermes serve`) keeps a SQLite handle open to `<profile>/memory_store.db` for **every** known profile — including brand-new empty ones. Both the CLI path (`hermes profile delete <name> -y`) and the Desktop UI path (Bot Mode right-click → Delete, which routes through `host.deleteProfile` → Electron-intercepted `DELETE /api/profiles/<name>`) hit the same lock.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch the Hermes Desktop app (it spawns `python -m hermes_cli.main serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0` as its backend).
2. Create a profile, e.g. via Bot Mode → New Agent (or Duplicate). A `default-2` profile with zero sessions is enough.
3. From a terminal run `hermes profile delete default-2 -y` — **or** in the Desktop UI right-click the bot → Delete → confirm.
4. Both fail. CLI output ends with:

```
✓ Stopped 2 profile backend process(es)
⚠ Could not remove C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\default-2: [WinError 32] 另一个程序正在使用此文件，进程无法访问。: 'C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\hermes\profiles\default-2\memory_store.db'
RuntimeError: Could not remove profile directory ...
```

The Desktop UI shows the same file-in-use error.

## Expected Behavior

Deleting a profile should succeed, or the app should explicitly tell the user a restart is required and/or release the file handles it holds on that profile.

## Root Cause (verified locally)

- The file lock is held by the **desktop's main backend** (`hermes serve`, verified via the Restart Manager API — `RmRegisterResources` on `memory_store.db` returns that single process for both `default-2` and `default-3`).
- That serve process opens `memory_store.db` (memory store) for **all known profiles** at startup — the empty, never-used `default-2` also has its memory_store.db held open.
- The desktop's delete path has interception logic precisely to avoid delete failures (see `apps/desktop/electron/profile-delete-routing.ts`, `ProfileDeletionGate`, fixing #52279): it tears down the *target profile's* pool/primary backend and routes follow-up requests away from it. But it does **not** close the *main serve process's* memory-store connections, so on Windows the `rmtree` still hits an open handle and fails.
- On POSIX, unlinking an open file succeeds, which is why #52279's fix appears to work on macOS; on Windows the open handle makes the delete fail hard. This is likely a Windows-only manifestation of the same deletion problem family.

## Additional Observations

- `hermes profile delete` reports `✓ Stopped 2 profile backend process(es)` yet the lock remains (serve keeps running — it is the desktop's own backend and must not be torn down).
- Workaround used locally: kill the `serve` chain processes (matched by command line `serve --host`) first, then delete — but this drops the desktop connection / requires an app restart, so it is not a real fix.

## Related

- #52279 "Deleted profile respawns indefinitely, accumulating zombie backend processes" — same deletion problem family, fixed on macOS side; this report is the Windows file-lock variant.

items.title: Desktop: sleep the pixel egg animation while it rests
items.body:
## Problem

`PixelEggSprite` schedules a new `requestAnimationFrame` before checking its state. In `bounce` mode the egg deliberately rests on frame 0 for 2.6–6.2 seconds between short bounce cycles, but the renderer still wakes at display cadence throughout each rest. In `hatch` mode it continues scheduling frames after the terminal frame has been drawn and `onDone` has fired.

This is unnecessary main-thread work, and can multiply in the draft grid where several eggs are mounted.

## Proposed fix

Schedule a timeout for long rest windows and request animation frames only while a visible bounce or hatch frame is due. Stop scheduling entirely after the final hatch frame. Preserve the existing animation timing, staggered first bounce, and canvas rendering behavior.

## Evidence

The affected loop is in `apps/desktop/src/components/pet/pixel-egg-sprite.tsx`. The production desktop investigation found residual renderer CPU after disabling the separately tracked Bots plugin workload; this component has a statically verifiable 60 Hz idle loop regardless of actual drawing work.

items.title: Desktop: pause the diffusion placeholder when the window is inactive
items.body:
## Problem

`DiffusionCanvas` continuously redraws the full image-generation placeholder with `requestAnimationFrame` while an image is pending. Unlike other Desktop renderer loops, it does not observe the shared window visibility/focus pause policy, so it continues drawing when the application is hidden, minimized, or unfocused.

## Proposed fix

Use the existing `createRendererLoopPauseController` in `DiffusionCanvas`: cancel the pending frame when the renderer is not observable and schedule a new frame on resume. Keep the current frame-by-frame rendering behavior while the active window is visible and focused.

## Evidence

The loop is at `apps/desktop/src/components/chat/image-generation-placeholder.tsx`. The shared pause mechanism is already used by other renderer loops and CSS animations (`apps/desktop/src/lib/renderer-loop-pause.ts`), but this canvas loop is not currently wired to it.

items.title: Multiplex: adapter-level session keys omit the profile, so all bots share one agent:main lane

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

In a multiplexed gateway, adapter-level session keys are derived **before** the runner stamps
`source.profile`, so every bot falls back to the *active* profile's namespace. For a Telegram DM —
where `chat.id` **is the user's own id**, identical across bots — all profiles therefore derive
the same `agent:main:telegram:dm:<uid>` key and share one lane.

This is the common root cause behind the three symptoms in #87239 and the collapsed-session
behaviour in #74285: those describe recovery/delivery/listing consequences, while this is the
ingress-side key that makes the collision possible in the first place.

Verified on a live 2-profile × 2-Telegram-bot gateway (v0.19.x, Windows, Python 3.11).

## Evidence

`gateway.log`, one full day of traffic across both bots:

```
$ grep -c "Flushing.*agent:medicina:" gateway.log   → 0
$ grep -c "Flushing.*agent:main:"     gateway.log   → 60
```

Zero keys carry the secondary profile's namespace. Both adapters — distinguishable in the logs by
their plugin logger (`telegram_platform.adapter` = default, `telegram_platform__home_<hash>.adapter`
= secondary) — emit the *same* key:

```
08:16:21  bot=MEDICINA  key=agent:main:telegram:dm:8693894969
08:21:08  bot=DEFAULT   key=agent:main:telegram:dm:8693894969
08:34:30  bot=MEDICINA  key=agent:main:telegram:dm:8693894969
08:50:02  bot=DEFAULT   key=agent:main:telegram:dm:8693894969
```

Reproduced in isolation against the current `main` code path:

```python
from gateway.session import SessionSource, build_session_key
src = SessionSource(platform=Platform.TELEGRAM, chat_id=UID, chat_type="dm", user_id=UID)

class Store:  # GatewaySessionStore._resolve_profile_for_key, multiplex on
    def _resolve_profile_for_key(self, source=None):
        if source is not None and getattr(source, "profile", None):
            return source.profile
        return "default"          # ← falls back to the ACTIVE profile

# base.py:5982 for BOTH adapters — source.profile is not yet stamped at ingress
print(build_session_key(src, profile=Store()._resolve_profile_for_key(src)))
# agent:main:telegram:dm:8693894969   (default bot)
print(build_session_key(src, profile=Store()._resolve_profile_for_key(src)))
# agent:main:telegram:dm:8693894969   (secondary bot — IDENTICAL)
```

## Root cause

Ordering. `BasePlatformAdapter.handle_message` (`gateway/platforms/base.py:5982`) derives the key
at ingress:

```python
profile=_sk_store._resolve_profile_for_key(event.source) if _sk_store else None,
```

`_resolve_profile_for_key` (`gateway/session.py:1764`) prefers `source.profile` and otherwise
falls back to `get_active_profile_name()`. But `source.profile` is stamped **later**, by
`GatewayRunner._make_profile_message_handler` (`gateway/run.py:15109`):

```python
async def _handler(event):
    if getattr(event, "source", None) is not None and not event.source.profile:
        event.source.profile = profile_name        # ← after the adapter already keyed
```

The adapter is the only component that knows which credential received the message, and at that
moment it has no way to say so. Consequences, all keyed on that one string:

- `_pending_text_batches` / `_pending_text_batch_tasks` — a secondary bot's message can be
  concatenated into the default bot's pending batch, and the flush task for one key cancels the
  other's.
- `_active_sessions` + the busy-session guard (`base.py:6126`) — a turn running for one profile
  makes the *other* profile's bot appear busy; `/stop` and `/new` cross profiles.
- `_post_delivery_callbacks`, `_photo_batch_key` (`:album:`, `:photo-burst` suffixes) — same
  collision.

Note this is not Telegram-specific. Every adapter's `_text_batch_key` has the same shape; the
Telegram DM is simply the case where the peer tuple is guaranteed identical. `feishu._media_batch_key`,
`raft` and `slack._session_key_for_source` additionally pass **no** `profile=` at all, so they stay
in `agent:main:` even once the source *is* stamped.

## Suggested fix

Give the adapter an explicit owner and one resolution seam, then route every call site through it.

```python
# BasePlatformAdapter
def set_owner_profile(self, profile_name):
    name = (profile_name or "").strip() or None
    self._owner_profile = None if name == "default" else name

def _session_key_profile(self, source=None):
    """source.profile → _owner_profile → session-store resolver."""
    stamped = getattr(source, "profile", None) if source is not None else None
    if stamped:
        return stamped
    if self._owner_profile:
        return self._owner_profile
    resolver = getattr(getattr(self, "_session_store", None), "_resolve_profile_for_key", None)
    ...
```

`GatewayRunner._configure_profile_adapter` calls `set_owner_profile(profile_name)` alongside the
other handler installs — before any inbound event can be processed, and on the reconnect path too,
since it shares that helper. Stamped sources keep priority so relay/connector ingress (which
legitimately routes per event, not per credential) is unaffected.

Byte-compatible where it matters: a primary adapter has no owner and an unstamped source, so it
resolves exactly as before (`agent:main:`); with `multiplex_profiles` off the resolver returns
`None` and every key is identical to today's.

## Testing

I have this implemented locally with a 12-case suite
(`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_adapter_session_key_namespace.py`) covering the collision itself,
stamped-source priority, primary/single-profile byte-compatibility, `"default"`/blank
normalisation, absent store, resolver exceptions, and `source=None` call sites. All 12 green;
135 green across the multiplex/profile/session suites
(`test_multiplex_adapter_registry`, `test_multiplex_profile_authz`, `test_profile_resolution`,
`test_profile_routing`, `test_multiplex_phase0`, `test_session`, `test_multiplex_http_routing`).

Happy to open a PR — say the word and whether you'd prefer the fix limited to
`base.py` + `run.py` or extended to the four adapters that currently pass no `profile=` at all
(feishu media, raft, slack) as I have it.

## Version

`main` @ `0c3452bf75`, Python 3.11, Windows 11. 2 profiles × 2 Telegram bot tokens, one gateway,
`gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, same user allowlisted on both.

Related: #87239 (delivery/listing symptoms), #74285 (session adoption), #88381 (durable
`profile_name` mislabel).

items.body:
I run a fork of hermes-agent, and Install & Update E2E fails on every scheduled run. As far as I can tell it can't pass on any fork, so it seemed worth reporting rather than being something specific to my setup.

`pick-releases` runs `scripts/sandbox/pick-release-tags.sh` to pick which releases to update FROM. A fork has no release tags of its own, so the script exits 1:

```
error: no release tags found in /home/runner/work/hermes-agent/hermes-agent
       A shallow clone has no tags: fetch with tags (actions/checkout
       with fetch-depth: 0, or fetch-tags: true).
```

That message sent me to the checkout first, and it's not the cause here. The job already uses `fetch-tags: true`. The tag list is empty because the fork genuinely has no tags and no releases.

The script looks right to me as written. On your repo an empty tag list really would mean the checkout lost its tags, and an empty matrix would silently cover nothing. The trouble is that from inside the script a fork looks identical to that fault.

The cron is `20 7,19 * * *`, so it's two failed runs a day on a fork plus the notification noise.

Four workflows already carry `if: github.repository == 'NousResearch/hermes-agent'` (`skills-index`, `skills-index-freshness`, `deploy-site`, `docker`), so my guess is this one was just missed. If that's right, the same line on `pick-releases` should do it, since `update` and `installer` both `needs:` it and skip with it.

I'm happy to open the PR if that's useful. I may well be missing a reason forks should keep running this one.

Hermes Desktop, connecting to a remote gateway (Raspberry Pi 5, hermes-agent)
3 real profiles confirmed via hermes profile list: default, coder, planner

items.title: Desktop user messages injected into zombie cron session (end_session not guaranteed on failure)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

When a cron job's execution fails (e.g., `RuntimeError: Connection error`) but the scheduler's `end_session()` call in the `finally` block doesn't complete (process crash, connection drop), the cron session stays open with `ended_at = NULL` and `end_reason` unset. The desktop app's sidebar **Cron Jobs section** renders this zombie session as a clickable run tile (`onOpenRun` → `onResumeSession`), and clicking it (or auto-selecting it) routes subsequent **desktop user messages into the cron session** instead of a new desktop session.

This caused a real incident: a cron agent that failed to find `x_search` (due to MCP tool namespace pollution) sat idle for 8 hours as a zombie, then received 11 user desktop messages about unrelated bot setup work. The cron agent executed the user's requests — creating profiles, editing config, writing ADR docs — all inside a `source = "cron"` session that was supposed to be dead.

## Root Cause

Two separate issues compound:

### 1. `end_session()` not guaranteed on cron failure

`cron/scheduler.py` line ~5854 calls `_session_db.end_session(_final_cron_session_id, "cron_complete")` in a `finally` block, but this is wrapped in `except (Exception, KeyboardInterrupt)` with only a `logger.debug`. When the cron process is killed by the inactivity watchdog (`HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT`) or crashes on a `Connection error`, the session DB close may never execute. The session remains `ended_at = NULL` in `state.db` until the desktop's `ws_orphan_reap` mechanism eventually catches it (which can take hours — it only fires on WebSocket reconnect/app restart).

### 2. Desktop sidebar allows resuming zombie cron sessions as chat

`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.tsx` renders cron run sessions as clickable tiles with `onOpenRun → onResumeSession`. There is no guard checking whether the cron session is actually still alive (`ended_at IS NULL` ≠ "active" when the session was never properly closed). Clicking the tile resumes the session as if it were a normal desktop chat, and the composer routes new user messages to it.

## Reproduction

1. Have a cron job scheduled (e.g., `30 8 * * *`)
2. Simulate a provider failure that causes the cron execution to crash/timeout (e.g., `RuntimeError: Connection error`) before `end_session()` runs
3. Observe: the cron session in `state.db` has `ended_at = NULL`, `end_reason = NULL` (not `cron_complete`)
4. Open the desktop app → sidebar → Cron Jobs section → expand the job → click the failed run
5. Type a message in the composer → it goes to the cron session, not a new desktop session
6. The cron agent (if still alive in the gateway process) responds and acts on the message

## Evidence (v0.20.2, commit `cf64ca20c`)

### Zombie cron session
```
session_id:    cron_4c76fda7ec90_20260817_084410
source:        cron
end_reason:    ws_orphan_reap  (NOT cron_complete — the finally block never ran)
started_at:    2026-08-17 08:44:17 +08:00
ended_at:      2026-08-17 17:16:56 +08:00  (8+ hours later, by desktop reaper)
message_count: 291
tool_calls:    151
```

### Cron execution record (executions.db)
```
id:          c4fb2e55cfe84422a9d22226dc7ce580
status:      failed
started_at:  2026-08-17T08:44:10+08:00
finished_at: 2026-08-17T09:00:27+08:00
error:       RuntimeError: Connection error.
```

### Injected desktop user messages (8 messages, 15:02–16:09)
All sent to `session_id = cron_4c76fda7ec90_20260817_084410` (source = cron):
- `2026-08-17 15:02` — model switch notification
- `2026-08-17 15:03` — skill invocation (grill-with-docs)
- `2026-08-17 15:13` — user: "q1:我觉得可以；q2:..." (bot profile setup decisions)
- `2026-08-17 15:21` — user: "q7:weibo-boss；q8:对的..."
- `2026-08-17 15:26` — skill invocation (writing-for-agents)
- `2026-08-17 15:28` — user: "这些都可以去检查一下..."
- `2026-08-17 15:50` — skill invocation (think)
- `2026-08-17 15:56` — user: "这个mcp目前来说只在flomo才用得上..."
- `2026-08-17 16:09` — user: "1、我想把flomo mcp从default中撤掉..."

The cron agent executed all of this: created `weibo-boss` and `flomo-boss` profiles, removed flomo MCP from default config, wrote ADR docs — all inside a cron session.

### Also observed on 2026-08-16
```
session_id: cron_4c76fda7ec90_20260816_084911
status:     failed (TimeoutError: idle for 702s)
end_reason: ws_orphan_reap (NOT cron_complete)
injected:   1 user message at 11:56 ("继续你的任务")
```

## Expected Behavior

1. When a cron execution fails, the session should be **guaranteed closed** with `end_reason = "cron_failed"` (or similar), not left as `ended_at = NULL` for the desktop reaper to eventually find.
2. The desktop sidebar should **not allow resuming a cron session that was never properly closed** (or any `source = cron` session at all — cron sessions are autonomous, not interactive chat targets). At minimum, clicking a cron run should open it read-only, not route new messages to it.

## Suggested Fixes

### Fix 1: Guarantee session close on cron failure
Add a hard guarantee in the cron scheduler that `end_session` is called even when the `finally` block's try/except swallows the error. Options:
- Use `atexit` or a signal handler to ensure `end_session` runs on process termination
- Add a startup sweep that closes any `source = cron` sessions with `ended_at IS NULL` from previous runs
- Write `end_reason = "cron_failed"` before the `finally` block, not only `"cron_complete"` on success

### Fix 2: Guard cron session resume in desktop
In `cron-jobs-section.tsx`, either:
- Disable `onOpenRun` for sessions with `ended_at IS NULL` (ambiguous state — could be in-progress or zombie)
- Open cron run sessions as **read-only** (view transcript, no composer)
- Or route the click to a new desktop session that references the cron run, rather than resuming the cron session itself

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.20.2 (2026.8.16), commit `cf64ca20c`
- macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)
- Desktop app (Electron)
- Provider: ollama-cloud (deepseek-v4-flash:0731)

## Workaround Applied

Set `tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled: true`, `cron.inflight_max_minutes: 15`, and `HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT=300` to shorten the zombie window, but this doesn't prevent the root cause.

items.title: [Bug]: Cron jobs cannot use Mnemosyne tools even when `hermes-mnemosyne` is enabled and the job requests the `memory`/`mnemosyne` toolsets

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
### Bug Description

# Summary
`cron/scheduler.py` unconditionally disables the `memory` toolset and passes `skip_memory=True` to `AIAgent` for every cron job. This prevents Mnemosyne-backed cron jobs (e.g. a weekly "memory harvest") from accessing `mnemosyne_remember`, `mnemosyne_triple_add`, `mnemosyne_remember_canonical`, etc., even when:

- `hermes-mnemosyne` is enabled (`hermes plugins enable hermes-mnemosyne`),
- `memory.provider: mnemosyne` is set in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`,
- the cron job explicitly requests `"memory"` and/or `"mnemosyne"` in `enabled_toolsets`.






### Steps to Reproduce

## Reproduction

1. Enable the plugin:
   ```bash
   hermes plugins enable hermes-mnemosyne
   ```

2. Create a cron job that needs Mnemosyne write tools:
   ```python
   cronjob(
       action='create',
       name='Weekly Memory Harvest',
       schedule='0 5 * * 1',
       skills=['memory-harvest'],
       enabled_toolsets=['session_search', 'memory', 'mnemosyne', 'file'],
       prompt='... harvest durable facts from recent sessions into Mnemosyne ...',
   )
   ```

3. Wait for the scheduled run (or trigger manually with `hermes cron run <job_id>`).

4. The job reports that all Mnemosyne tools are unavailable and writes zero facts:
   > Weekly Memory Harvest — failed  
   > 0 facts/triples written because Mnemosyne tools are still not exposed in this cron session, even though hermes-mnemosyne is enabled in ~/.hermes/config.yaml.  
   > Blocker: mnemosyne_remember_canonical, mnemosyne_triple_add, mnemosyne_remember, mnemosyne_stats are all unavailable via tool_search in the cron session.


### Expected Behavior

Cronjob Response: Weekly Memory Harvest
(job_id: 39c7bd2028a9)
-------------

Weekly Memory Harvest — success

3 canonical facts written:
...redacted...
4 knowledge triples written:
...redacted...
6 non-cron sessions reviewed (Aug 10–12); none found Aug 13–17.
Blocker resolved: Mnemosyne tools are now available in cron after the scheduler patch/gateway restart.

### Actual Behavior

Cronjob Response: Weekly Memory Harvest
(job_id: 39c7bd2028a9)
-------------

Weekly Memory Harvest — failed

0 facts/triples written because Mnemosyne tools are still not exposed in this cron session, even though hermes-mnemosyne is enabled in ~/.hermes/config.yaml.
Blocker: mnemosyne_remember_canonical, mnemosyne_triple_add, mnemosyne_remember, mnemosyne_stats are all unavailable via tool_search in the cron session. The gateway/cron worker likely needs a restart to pick up the enabled plugin.

### Affected Component

Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (CLI only)

### Debug Report

```shell
Report       https://paste.rs/0X6Sd
agent.log    https://paste.rs/dvWk1
gateway.log  https://paste.rs/KxJ7U
```

### Operating System

Ubuntu 24.04.4

### Python Version

Python 3.11.15 (Hermes venv)

### Hermes Version

0.20.1

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

In `cron/scheduler.py`:

1. `_resolve_cron_disabled_toolsets()` always adds `"memory"` to the disabled list, regardless of the job's `enabled_toolsets`.
2. The `AIAgent` constructed for the cron job is hard-coded with `skip_memory=True`.

Mnemosyne tools are surfaced by the `hermes-mnemosyne` memory provider, so `skip_memory=True` prevents the provider from initializing and the tools from being registered. Disabling the `memory` toolset removes them even if they were registered. A gateway restart alone does not help because the scheduler module keeps these hard-coded defaults.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

### Change 1 — `_resolve_cron_disabled_toolsets`
Only add `"memory"` to the disabled list when the resolved `enabled_toolsets` does **not** contain `"memory"` or `"mnemosyne"`.

```python
def _resolve_cron_disabled_toolsets(
    cfg: dict,
    enabled_toolsets: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    requested = {str(t).strip().lower() for t in (enabled_toolsets or [])}
    cron_cfg = (cfg or {}).get("cron") or {}
    if cron_cfg.get("allow_agent_scheduling"):
        disabled = ["messaging", "clarify"]
    else:
        disabled = ["cronjob", "messaging", "clarify"]
    if not (requested & {"memory", "mnemosyne"}):
        disabled.append("memory")
    ...
```

### Change 2 — `AIAgent` construction
Compute `skip_memory` from the resolved toolsets instead of hard-coding `True`.

```python
_enabled_toolsets = _resolve_cron_enabled_toolsets(job, _cfg)
_disabled_toolsets = _resolve_cron_disabled_toolsets(_cfg, _enabled_toolsets)
_skip_memory = not any(
    t in ("memory", "mnemosyne") for t in (_enabled_toolsets or [])
)

agent = AIAgent(
    ...
    enabled_toolsets=_enabled_toolsets,
    disabled_toolsets=_disabled_toolsets,
    skip_memory=_skip_memory,
    ...
)
```

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop Cron list is empty in SSH connection mode — cron REST requests lack connectionId on the primary path
items.body:
### Summary

Hermes Desktop in **SSH connection mode** shows an empty Cron list ("No cronjobs") even though the remote backend — the one the chat session is actually talking to — has plenty of jobs. Chat and sessions work fine; only REST requests for cron data route to the wrong backend.

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.20.2 (2026.8.16) on both sides
- Desktop: Windows native app, connection mode `ssh` (`connections.json`: `primary: wsl-hermes`, kind `ssh`)
- Remote: WSL Linux, `hermes serve` dialed through the SSH tunnel (reused from the previous session: `reusing remote dashboard pid=2429 port=37089`)
- Local pool backend: on boot the desktop main process also spawns a Windows-native `hermes serve --profile default` (observed `HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=62503`), and that instance has **no `cron/jobs.json` at all** (expected here — it is a dual-instance setup where the Windows side intentionally keeps cron empty so jobs do not double-run; the 18 real jobs live under WSL `~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json`)

### Reproduction steps

1. Configure Desktop connection mode = SSH to a remote Hermes that has cron jobs (e.g. WSL via `localhost:22`, key auth).
2. Confirm the remote backend has jobs in its `cron/jobs.json` (`hermes cron list` on the remote shows them).
3. Open the Desktop Cron page / sidebar "Cron jobs" section.
4. Observed: empty list ("No cronjobs"). Chat/sessions against the same remote backend work normally.
5. Switching connections (local ↔ ssh) does not help — the bug is on the primary path, which is immune to connection switching.

### Root cause

The renderer cron helpers tag their REST request with `connectionScoped()` (`apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts`), but the connection id comes from `activeGatewayConnectionId()` (`apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts:168`), which returns `null` whenever `activeKey === primaryProfile` — unconditionally, under the assumption that "primary == local pool". In SSH mode the primary gateway *is* the remote connection, so the cron request ships without `connectionId`; the main process `handleHermesApiRequest` (`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`) only takes the registry branch when `apiRequestRegistryConnectionId()` is non-null, and with a null id it falls through to the legacy local-profile route → `ensureBackend("default")` → the **local** backend (empty cron) → empty list.

Field evidence matching this chain:

- `desktop.log`: `Starting Hermes backend for profile "default" via Hermes at C:\Users\...\hermes-agent` + `HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=62503` + `could not read served dashboard token ... 404 Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled`
- `backend-ownership.json` registers profile `default` to that Windows-local serve process (`--profile default serve`)
- Probing `127.0.0.1:62503/api/status` returns live v0.20.2 (the empty-cron backend); the remote WSL serve on the tunnel port holds the real jobs

### Why the neighboring fixes do not cover this

- #87882 / #88000 (merged: "read cron run-history from the owning gateway") added **connection routing** — it makes a tagged request reach the right host, but it still depends on the request carrying a `connectionId`. On the primary path `activeGatewayConnectionId()` returns null, so the tag never arrives and the request never enters the registry branch.
- #82530 / #88067 (merged today: "map SSH profile aliases in cron/REST profile filters") fixes the **profile parameter translation** inside the registry branch (`?profile=local-alias` → remote namespace). Same premise: the request must already be registry-routed. A primary-path request with no `connectionId` bypasses that branch entirely.

Both fixes operate downstream of the bug reported here. The gap is one line:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts:168 — current upstream main
export function activeGatewayConnectionId(): null | string {
  if (g.activeKey === g.primaryProfile) {
    return null          // primary is assumed to be the local pool
  }
  return g.secondaries.get(g.activeKey)?.connectionId ?? null
}
```

### Suggested fix

Make the primary path aware of its connection source:

```ts
export function activeGatewayConnectionId(): null | string {
  if (g.activeKey === g.primaryProfile) {
    // In SSH/remote mode the primary IS a registry connection; only a
    // genuinely local primary should resolve to the local pool.
    return g.primaryConnectionId ?? null
  }
  return g.secondaries.get(g.activeKey)?.connectionId ?? null
}
```

with `setPrimaryGateway()` (`apps/desktop/src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.ts`) recording the source `connectionId` when the gateway came from a registered connection (the renderer already has `desktop.getConnectionFor({ connectionId, profile })` / `getGatewayWsUrlFor` used for secondaries — the same lookup should feed the primary). Alternatively, force the cron REST helpers to always carry the active registry connection id, independent of the primary/secondary distinction.

items.title: fix(desktop): HUD toggle leaves no surface when main window is hidden or minimized at open time (retry)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Summary

Toggling HUD mode off (`Ctrl+Shift+H` or the titlebar button) closes the HUD
**and the main chat window** in a sequence that leaves the user with no
visible Hermes surface. Reproducible 100% on Windows when the main window is
not the foreground-visible window at the moment HUD mode is entered
(minimized, hidden behind another app, or focused elsewhere is enough).

### Environment

- Hermes Agent CLI: v0.20.1 (2026.8.13)
- Hermes Desktop build: 40.10.2 (`apps/desktop/package.json`, built 2026-08-15)
- OS: Windows 11
- Repro count on this machine: 2/2 attempts, same shape each time

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Hermes Desktop. Main window opens, visible.
2. Click on any other app to defocus the main window (or minimize it).
3. Press `Ctrl+Shift+H` to enter HUD mode. HUD window appears, main window
   hides as expected.
4. Press `Ctrl+Shift+H` again to leave HUD mode. **HUD closes. Main window
   does not reappear.** The user is left with no Hermes surface at all;
   Hermes.exe processes keep running with no visible main window.
5. The only way back is killing the HUD-window PID and waiting for the main
   process tree to respawn the main window, or restarting the app.

### Expected

Leaving HUD mode restores the main window to the visibility state it had
before HUD mode was entered (visible if it was visible, hidden if it was
hidden — but never *lost*).

### Actual

The main window stays hidden after HUD closes. In my repro the main window
process tree actually collapses: post-fix `Get-Process Hermes` shows no
window with title `"Hermes"`, only the orphaned HUD window (which is
re-labelled as the main process's window in the second cycle).

### Where the bug is

`apps/desktop/electron/main.ts`, the HUD section around lines 10440–10895.
Specifically:

**Line 10835** — `openHudWindow` snapshots the restore decision:

```ts
hudRestoreMainWindow = Boolean(
  mainWindow && !mainWindow.isDestroyed() && mainWindow.isVisible()
)
```

This is the smoking gun. The restore flag is `true` **only if the main window
is currently visible at HUD-open time**. If the main window is minimized,
hidden, or behind another app at that moment, the flag stays `false` and
`restoreMainWindowFromHud()` (line 10783) no-ops at line 10785–10787.

**Line 14328–14333** — sibling bypass. There's an app-quit path that calls
`hudWindow.destroy()` with `'closed'` listeners removed to avoid a re-entrant
restore, but the comment on line 14328 itself says
"(`hudRestoreMainWindow` may still be armed from entering HUD)" — yet the
bypass doesn't restore anything itself. A normal HUD close via the toggle
shouldn't hit this path, but it's an indication the team was aware the
restore decision was brittle.

### Why it's the wrong design

`hudRestoreMainWindow` is recorded *once*, at open time, as a snapshot. The
flag then survives the lifetime of the HUD window. If the snapshot is wrong
— because the user happened to minimize first, or focus moved, or the
desktop was already in some weird state — there is no recovery: closing HUD
silently fails to restore.

The intent (per the comment at line 10453–10456) is to avoid raising a main
window the user had already minimized. That intent is fine; the
implementation is too narrow. The flag should be either:

1. **Always set true** when entering HUD mode, and `restoreMainWindowFromHud`
   should call `mainWindow.show()` only when the prior visibility was
   actually `visible` (track the prior state separately from the restore
   decision), **or**
2. **Defensively try-and-log**: on HUD close, if `mainWindow` exists and is
   not destroyed, attempt `show()` regardless of the flag, and log if the
   flag was `false` so a regression surfaces in `rememberLog` instead of
   silently breaking the user's screen.

A test would help here too — `restoreMainWindowFromHud()` currently has no
coverage in `apps/desktop/electron/` (the only HUD test files are
`hud-snap-shortcut.test.ts` and `hud.test.ts` for the snap controller, not
the main-window restore branch).

### Diagnostic evidence from this session

Captured at the moment of bug, on the live system:

**Before the second toggle (HUD open):**
```
Id    MainWindowTitle  IsVisible
17772 Hermes HUD       True
[no Hermes window with title "Hermes" — main is hidden]
```

**After killing the HUD PID and waiting 1.5s (the only workaround):**
```
Id    MainWindowTitle  IsVisible
20156 Hermes           True
```
Main window respawned cleanly — confirming the process tree is healthy and
the bug is purely in the visibility-restoration branch, not in any process
crash.

UserData observation: `hud-state.json` is rewritten on every HUD close, so
deleting it before the next HUD open resets the window to default bounds.
Not relevant to this bug, just noting it as a side observation.

### Suggested fix direction (not a PR yet)

Smallest change that closes the bug:

- At line 10835, separate "should we restore?" from "what was the prior
  visibility?". Record `hudPriorMainWindowVisible` (or whatever name fits
  the existing style) alongside `hudRestoreMainWindow`, and let
  `restoreMainWindowFromHud` decide based on the prior visibility, not the
  flag.
- Defensive backstop: in `restoreMainWindowFromHud`, if `mainWindow` exists
  and is not destroyed, always at least call `show()` and let the OS
  no-op if the window was already visible. Log via `rememberLog` when the
  flag was `false` so silent regressions surface in
  `~/.hermes/logs/desktop.log`.

Happy to send a PR with the test + fix once we agree on direction.

### Why this matters

HUD mode is a load-bearing feature for the desktop app's "agent buddy while
you work in another app" pitch (Tonbi's 2026-08-17 demo, the README's
quick-start, the docs at hermes-agent.nousresearch.com). A toggle that
silently destroys the user's main window on the second press is a
**regression class**, not a one-off — any user who minimizes the app first
will hit it. The fix needs to ship before HUD mode is treated as
production-ready.

items.title: Bug: a profile's sessions are physically stored in the default/root state.db (profile_name correct) — desktop shows them under the default/hermes bot

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description

On a multi-profile host with a **single multiplexed gateway** (`gateway.run.multiplex_profiles: true`), an agent session for profile **fitness** (reached via its own Feishu bot) is **physically stored in the default/root `state.db`**, not in that profile's own store. The session's `profile_name` column is set correctly (`fitness`), but the row lives in `~/.hermes/state.db` (the **default** root home) — and the desktop app then **shows the fitness session under the default/hermes bot**.

Environment:
- OS: Windows 11, Hermes installed via git (v0.20.2-lineage; HEAD ~2026-08-17), Hermes Desktop
- Single gateway: `hermes gateway run` with `gateway.run.multiplex_profiles: true` (one process serves both default and fitness Feishu bots)
- Profiles: `default`, `fitness`, `llm-wiki`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run one default gateway with `multiplex_profiles: true` so it serves both the default and the fitness Feishu bots.
2. In Feishu, DM the **fitness** bot (a dm / p2p conversation).
3. Inspect `~/.hermes/state.db` (the **default root** store):

```
sqlite> SELECT id, profile_name, chat_id, chat_type FROM sessions WHERE id='20260817_233028_542fda58';
20260817_233028_542fda58 | fitness | oc_5484a... | dm
```

   The session is there with `profile_name='fitness'`. It exists in the default/root store.
4. Inspect `~/.hermes/profiles/fitness/state.db` — the same session is **absent**; that profile store only holds stale pre-upgrade rows.

## Expected Behavior

A session owned by profile `fitness` should live in **that profile's own store** (`~/.hermes/profiles/fitness/state.db`), matching the `profile_name` it carries — or, failing that (single shared store), the desktop UI must render it under the **fitness** bot, never under default/hermes.

## Impact

This breaks the profile physical-isolation the user relies on (`default` root home being shared/fallback while also holding default's own data), and produces visibly wrong ownership in the desktop UI (a fitness DM appears under the hermes/default bot). Data is not lost and delivery works, but ownership/display is misleading.

## Notes / Related

- This is the "session storage" concrete symptom of #76584 ([Feature]: Decouple the default profile from the global root HERMES_HOME), where `default` is a hardcoded alias for the root `~/.hermes`, making "fallback to default" indistinguishable from a leak.
- Sibling concrete symptom, filed separately in the same spirit: #76393 (terminal env snapshot clobbers multi-profile session isolation).
- Behavior regressed around the v0.20-lineage update: sessions for `fitness` were stored in `~/.hermes/profiles/fitness/state.db` before 2026-08-16, and started landing in the root store after.

## Repro session id (for maintainers)

`20260817_233028_542fda58` — Feishu DM to the fitness bot; `profile_name='fitness'`, `source='feishu'`, `chat_type='dm'`, physically in `~/.hermes/state.db`.

items.title: Desktop: top session tab bar disappears and does not persist across restarts/updates

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description
The top session tab bar (the stacked session tiles over the chat) can disappear entirely and not come back across app restarts/updates. Reported alongside #88531, but it is a **separate defect** from the PROJECTS-collapse bug (that one was repo discovery in remote mode; this one is session-tile/layout persistence).

## Steps to Reproduce
- Have multiple session tabs open in the top tab bar (e.g. ~5).
- Click one or two of them.
- The whole tab bar disappears. Sessions are NOT lost — they still appear under the flat Recents / "Show all profiles" list. Only the tab bar is gone.
- The tab bar stays gone across app restarts and an app update.

## Expected Behavior
Clicking a session tab switches to that tab. The tab bar should persist its open tabs across restarts.

## Actual Behavior
The tab bar vanished and does not return after restart or app update.

## On-disk evidence (Aug 17)
Read the app's persisted state at ~/Library/Application Support/Hermes/Local Storage:
- `hermes.desktop.sessionTiles.v2` is **absent** — the session tiles for the active profile are not persisted. `$sessionTiles` is keyed per gateway profile (`store/session-states.ts:574`) and hydrates from this key on restart; absent key = no tabs.
- `hermes.desktop.layoutTree.v2` exists, and the workspace group carries panes `["sessions", "workspace", "review", "terminal"]` — **no session tiles** in it. The top tab bar is the workspace group's `headerHidden` state + the tiles stacked in it; both show nothing to restore.
- The project-filter atom (`hermes.desktop.sidebarProjectFilter`) is absent — the PROJECTS collapse is NOT this bug (that was remote-mode repo discovery, see #88531).

## Where the state lives (from source, not a confirmed trigger)
- Tab bar visibility = workspace group `headerHidden` (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/session-tile.tsx:557`, `setTreeGroupHeaderHidden`), or a layout reset (`stackSessionTilesIntoMain` / `resetLayoutTree`) that re-collapses tiles into main as one strip.
- Session tiles are persisted separately under `TILES_KEY = 'hermes.desktop.sessionTiles.v2'` keyed per profile (`store/session-states.ts:503-574`).

The exact trigger that wiped the persisted tiles is not yet pinned. Needs a maintainer to reproduce and confirm.

## Environment
- macOS desktop app (backend host)
- Desktop app running in remote mode against the backend
- Repo commit 4323c67dc

items.title: [Bug] Desktop: cross-profile bot switch intermittently lands on blank new-chat route (#/) instead of the target session

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

On a multi-profile Desktop setup, opening a **non-primary profile's** canonical chat from a desktop UI plugin (the Bot Mode "Bots" pane) intermittently lands on the blank new-chat route (`#/`) instead of the target session. The profile activates correctly, and the session route is written successfully — then a Desktop effect reverts the route to `#/` a moment later. It is a timing race tied to the profile/gateway connection switch, and it reproduces intermittently (works on some switches, fails on others).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Hermes Desktop (v0.20.2) with multiple profiles (a primary + one or more named profiles).
2. Open the Bots pane (the `hermes-bots` plugin loads a roster of profiles as "bots").
3. Click a non-primary bot → its canonical chat opens correctly.
4. Switch to a different bot/chat, then click the first bot again.
5. Repeat a few times.

**Actual:** intermittently the window ends on the blank home/new-chat screen (`#/`) with the profile pill showing the target profile, even though the target session exists and is valid.

**Expected:** the target bot's canonical chat opens every time.

## Root-cause analysis (instrumented)

I added a temporary diagnostic to the plugin around `host.openSession(id, { profile })`. The captured values across runs are decisive:

- Profile activation succeeds: the plugin reads the target profile as active (`active=marina`).
- The session route **is** written correctly. Immediately after the open, `location.hash` is the target session route (e.g. `#/20260816_171312_5a6f63`).
- Within ~300 ms the route reverts to `#/`.
- Adding a fixed 450 ms delay before the plugin's navigation did **not** help — the reset still fires afterward. This shows the reset is triggered by the gateway connection switch *completing* (variable timing, longer for a remote/secondary profile), not by a fixed window.

So the bug is a Desktop core race between two paths in the profile-switch flow and the session-open:

1. **Connection-switch handler clears session state.** `apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/wiring.tsx` (≈ lines 741–742):

   ```ts
   beforeConnectionSwitch: () => {
     startFreshSessionDraft({ preserveRoute: true, workspaceTarget: null })
     ...
   }
   ```

   `startFreshSessionDraft` clears `$activeSessionId` / `$selectedStoredSessionId` even with `preserveRoute` (see `app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts`).

2. **Route-resume effect then navigates to the blank route.** `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-route-resume.ts` (≈ lines 174–183):

   ```ts
   if (
     isNewChatRoute(locationPathname) &&
     !creatingSessionRef.current &&
     (selectedStoredSessionId || activeSessionId || !freshDraftReady) &&
     !rawHashLooksLikeSession()
   ) {
     bootResumeRef.current = false
     startFreshSessionDraft(true)   // navigates to NEW_CHAT_ROUTE (#/)
   }
   ```

The cross-profile open (plugin SDK `host.openSession(id, { profile })` → `ensureGatewayProfile` → `openSession` in `app/open-session.ts`, route decision at ≈ line 135) sets the correct session route, but the connection-switch/route-resume transitions above can run afterward and reset it to `#/`. Because the timing depends on when the secondary profile's gateway socket finishes dialing, the failure is intermittent.

## Evidence

- Instrumented plugin toasts confirmed: `active=<target>` (correct) while `route=#/` (wrong), with the correct session route observed momentarily before the revert.
- Target session verified valid: exists in the profile's `state.db`, not hidden/archived, with its messages intact.
- Reproduced on a clean build from the official `v2026.8.16` tag (see Environment).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent **v0.20.2** — tag `v2026.8.16`, commit `df4b65147d7ddd74dd449f9067aabbca5aef0ec7`
- macOS arm64, packaged Desktop app (`hermes desktop`)
- Multiple Hermes profiles; the target is a non-primary profile
- Plugin: `hermes-bots` (the standalone Bot Mode plugin) loaded from `~/.hermes/desktop-plugins/hermes-bots`, using the Desktop plugin SDK (`apps/desktop/src/sdk/index.ts`) `host.openSession(storedSessionId, { profile })`

## Notes

- The standalone Bot Mode plugin is believed to be using the supported SDK open path correctly; the same cross-profile open works when the primary profile is involved. The race appears specific to activating a secondary profile and immediately opening one of its stored sessions.
- This also matches the archived `NousResearch/Hermes-Bot-Mode` issues #40 ("Clicking a bot does not reliably switch/open its chat") and #22 ("Preserve canonical chats outside the recent-session page"), which were closed when Bot Mode moved into the Desktop codebase — the underlying profile-switch/session-routing race appears not to have been fully resolved in core.

items.title: [Bug]: core compression retries unchanged transcript after would_grow rejection

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Core automatic compression can repeatedly retry the same unchanged transcript after the generated compressed candidate is rejected because it is larger than the original.

The anti-growth safety guard correctly prevents data growth, but the rejection is not recorded by the existing anti-thrashing breaker.

## Observed behavior

Example:

- Original transcript: ~70,503 tokens
- Candidate compressed transcript: ~71,139 tokens
- Candidate growth: ~636 tokens

Hermes correctly preserves the original transcript and emits:

```text
Compression refused: compressed transcript would be larger than the original
```

On later turns, the unchanged transcript remains above the compression threshold, so automatic compression attempts again.

## Root cause

The `would_grow` rejection occurs in `agent/conversation_compression.py` after `ContextCompressor.compress()` returns.

The existing ineffective-compression counter lives in `agent/context_compressor.py`, but the `would_grow` path does not record an ineffective compaction verdict.

As a result:

1. The original transcript is preserved.
2. `_ineffective_compression_count` is unchanged.
3. The automatic breaker does not trip.
4. The same compression operation is retried on the next turn.

## Expected behavior

When automatic compression is rejected with `failure_class="would_grow"`:

- Preserve the original transcript unchanged.
- Record the attempt as an ineffective automatic compaction.
- Persist the existing anti-thrashing state.
- Stop repeated identical automatic retries after the normal breaker threshold.
- Allow manual compression to bypass the automatic deferral.
- Allow a fitting real-usage response or successful compaction to clear the state.
- Keep detailed diagnostics and telemetry.
- Avoid repeating a user-facing warning on every turn.

## Proposed direction

Add an explicit compressor method for a rejected, non-committed compaction, rather than calling the private counter method directly from the outer compression layer.

The method should increment the ineffective counter and set zero savings, but must not mark a compaction as committed or arm post-compaction real-usage verification.

## Related work

- #86700: never persist a compression that grows the transcript
- #79540: gateway hygiene compression loops while still above the hard limit
- #79876: proposed gateway cooldown for that condition
- #23811: compression inflates small sessions
- #15432: anti-thrashing recovery

This issue is related to those items but covers the core in-place `would_grow` path specifically.

items.title: design(kanban): compact board hierarchy and progressive task details

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Kanban has strong workflow semantics, but the current board presents setup, board administration, orchestration, attention, filtering, and daily task work at nearly the same visual level. This issue proposes a focused information architecture and density pass for Desktop and WebUI. It is a design-quality follow-up to #87244, not a replacement for that responsive usability fix.

The goal is simple: help an operator answer "what needs attention, who owns it, and what is blocked?" before exposing setup and executor detail.

## Jobs to be done

Frequent:
- scan lane state and find high-risk or stale work
- understand owner, age, dependencies, and active worker state
- open, create, move, and comment on tasks
- resolve attention and switch board or active filters
- preserve horizontal lane memory

Occasional or administrative:
- create or archive a board
- edit board settings
- configure orchestration
- inspect model, workspace, skills, goal mode, raw specification, or repository provenance

The present UI gives several occasional controls persistent top-level space and renders much executor metadata at the same weight as the task purpose.

## Proposed hierarchy

### Desktop board

```text
[global rail] [Board / 24 tasks] [Orchestrating / 3]  [Search] [Filters 2] [Attention 2] [...] [New task]
              [active filter chips]                                      [density / live state]
              Todo 5       Ready 3       In progress 4      Blocked 2       Review 3
              card         card          card               card            card
```

- Use one compact board header. Keep board switcher, task count, orchestration state, search, filters, attention count, and one `New task` primary action.
- Move Settings, New board, Archive, and manual Nudge into an overflow or board-admin menu.
- Replace the full attention region with a severity/count control that opens a focused rail.
- Show active filters as removable chips; keep filter construction in one popover.
- Start lanes directly below the header and filter row. Keep headers sticky with status, count, optional WIP, and add action.
- Keep horizontal board semantics. Empty lanes may collapse to a narrow rail, but must remain discoverable.
- Card order: title, machine or human risk state, owner, dependency signal, age. Hide long descriptions and internal IDs until open.
- Cream is reserved for the true primary action. Status colors carry semantic meaning only.

### Mobile board and task drawer

Use one focused, snap-aligned lane with an explicit lane selector and count. Open task details as a viewport-contained drawer.

Drawer hierarchy:
1. human summary: title, status, owner, urgency, blocker or outcome
2. concise purpose and acceptance conditions
3. full-width disclosure rows for `Execution details`, `Repository & provenance`, and `View specification`
4. attachments, comments, activity, and run history by task relevance
5. admin actions in overflow

The drawer should use one content grid and one gutter. Labels and values must align; values wrap only inside the value column. Paths use inset monospace blocks aligned to that grid. At 320, 360, 390, and 430px there must be no hanging labels, orphan separators, or arbitrary indentation. Disclosure rows and actions need at least 44px targets.

## Measurable acceptance criteria

| Measure | Current observed direction | Target |
|---|---:|---:|
| Board chrome before lanes at 900px height | multiple stacked control regions | lanes begin by 120px from board content top |
| Persistent primary-emphasis actions | several cream controls compete | exactly 1 primary action |
| Desktop board controls before overflow | setup and work mixed | 7 or fewer visible work controls |
| Visible cards at 1600x900 | low due to chrome and verbose cards | at least 4 compact cards in each populated lane without body scroll |
| Drawer metadata | inline wrapping / mixed alignment | stable label-value grid with one gutter |
| Touch targets | mixed | 44x44px minimum for primary controls and disclosures |
| Horizontal containment | right lanes and drawer can overflow | no page-level overflow at 320/360/390/430/768/1600px |
| Keyboard | partial pointer-first flow | search shortcut, lane/card navigation, open, move, create, close, and focus return |
| Accessibility | quiet secondary text and tiny controls are risky | WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, visible focus, semantic names, reduced-motion support |
| Performance | no explicit redesign budget | no new heavy UI framework; virtualize or incrementally render large lanes; avoid idle animation work |

## Interaction and accessibility details

- Preserve drag and drop on desktop, but provide menu and keyboard equivalents for every move.
- Return focus to the originating card when the drawer closes.
- Announce lane moves and filter result counts to assistive technology.
- Do not encode state by color alone.
- Mobile does not require drag and drop. Use explicit Move action plus snap navigation.
- Density may be `comfortable` and `compact` only if persisted per board; otherwise ship one well-tested compact default.

## Why this fits Hermes

The proposal keeps the existing dark-green and cream identity, system tokens, compact mono metadata, status tones, profile identity, live orchestration state, and horizontal workflow model. It changes prominence and grouping rather than importing another product's skin.

The current Desktop component boundaries already support a phased pass: `board.tsx`, `drawer.tsx`, `board-switcher.tsx`, `orchestration.tsx`, shared `ui.tsx`, and plugin tokens. WebUI should share the same behavioral contract even where rendering code remains separate.

## Research principles

- Progressive disclosure: [Carbon disclosure pattern](https://carbondesignsystem.com/components/accordion/usage/)
- Minimum target size and focus: [WCAG 2.2 target size](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html) and [focus appearance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-appearance.html)
- Board and table view customization: [GitHub Projects documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/planning-and-tracking-with-projects/customizing-views-in-your-project/customizing-the-board-layout)
- Keyboard-first command access: [Linear keyboard shortcuts](https://linear.app/docs/keyboard-shortcuts)
- Responsive layout and adaptive navigation: [Material 3 adaptive layouts](https://m3.material.io/foundations/layout/applying-layout/window-size-classes)

These are principle references only. The proposed visuals remain original and Hermes-native.

## Suggested phases

1. IA and board chrome: compact header, attention control, filters, lane headers, card hierarchy.
2. Task drawer: summary-first content grid and progressive disclosure of executor/provenance detail.
3. Mobile and keyboard: focused lane selector, drawer behavior, focus management, explicit move actions.
4. Density and scale: persisted density only if needed, large-board rendering budget, shared Desktop/WebUI behavior tests.

## Non-goals

- no Kanban state-machine or dispatcher changes
- no replacement for #87244
- no redesign of unrelated dashboard pages
- no new animation system or heavy component framework
- no hidden removal of diagnostics, provenance, runs, or raw task specifications

## Maintainer question

Would maintainers prefer the responsive and information-hierarchy contract to live in shared Kanban layout primitives used by Desktop and WebUI, or should the two surfaces keep separate renderers with shared behavior tests?

items.title: Bot Mode: bot-to-bot `chat -Q -q` sends run the receiving agent's turn but persist nothing

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug description

The Bots plugin instructs agents to message each other with:

```
hermes -p <agent-name> chat --in ~ -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q -q "Message from 🤖 <sender> (@<handle>): …"
```

(`apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/plugin.js`, the agent-facing instructions around the `GENERIC_TITLES` block.)

The receiving agent genuinely processes the turn — it can read files, verify claims, and produce a reply — but the exchange is **persisted nowhere**. The CLI banner reports resuming the canonical Bot Chat session, yet that session's stored history is unchanged afterward; the sent message text is findable only in `logs/agent.log`.

## Repro

1. Two profiles on one machine, gateway running (multiplex on in our case).
2. `hermes -p default chat --in ~ -c "Bot Chat" --create-if-missing -Q -q "Message from 🤖 worker (@worker): hello, please remember this"`
3. CLI prints `↻ Resumed session <id> "Bot Chat"` and the receiving agent's composed reply.
4. Inspect the session store: the resumed session's message rows/usage show no trace of this exchange; open the receiver's Bot Chat in the desktop — nothing new.
5. `grep -rl "hello, please remember this" ~/.hermes` → only `logs/agent.log`.

## Expected

A bot-to-bot message delivered "straight into the bot's ONE canonical Bot Chat" (the plugin's own wording) appears in that chat's persisted history, like any other turn.

## Actual

The turn is ephemeral. The receiving agent's canonical Bot Chat shows no trace in the desktop, so agent-to-agent knowledge transfer silently evaporates — it survives only if the receiving agent happens to write its own memory file during the turn, which is how we noticed the gap.

## Impact

Bot Mode's inter-agent messaging looks like it works (sender gets a reply) while the conversation history the feature is named after never materializes. Anything coordinated this way is unauditable after the fact.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.20.2 → reproduced again after updating to v0.20.3
- macOS (darwin), multiplex gateway, default + 3 named profiles
